claims.behaviour: ComparableTuple is a final class implementing Comparable<ComparableTuple> with no public constructor. Its public members are exactly: the constant NIL; the static factories of(long), of(double), of(String), of(String, String), of(long, long), of(String[]), of(Long[]), of(String, long), of(String, long, String) and of(java.util.List) each returning a ComparableTuple; and compareTo(ComparableTuple), equals(Object), hashCode() and toString().

of(long), of(double) and of(String) each return a one-element tuple holding the given value; of(long) and of(double) never throw (NaN and infinities are accepted), of(String) accepts the empty string but throws IllegalArgumentException when the string is null. With int literals, of(999) and of(-5) resolve to the long factory and hold integer numbers.

of(String, String), of(long, long), of(String, long) and of(String, long, String) return tuples of their arguments in argument order, e.g. of("x", 7, "y") holds the three elements "x", 7, "y". of(String, String) throws IllegalArgumentException if either string is null; of(String, long) if the string is null; of(String, long, String) if the first or the last string is null. of(long, long) never throws.

of(String[]) and of(Long[]) return a tuple of the array elements in order. The array is copied: changing the array after the call does not change the tuple (of(new String[]{"a","b"}) still equals of("a","b") after element 0 of the array is set to "z"). A null array throws IllegalArgumentException; an empty array gives an empty tuple equal to NIL. The tuple has no mutators, so it is immutable.

Null elements inside the array passed to of(String[]) or of(Long[]) are not rejected at creation (as the original does). Such a tuple later throws NullPointerException from hashCode() and when the null is compared against a number at the same position; toString() prints the null element as the text null.

of(java.util.List) builds a tuple from the list elements in order. Each element must be a String, any java.lang.Number, or a ComparableTuple; a nested ComparableTuple is flattened, its elements inserted in its place. Example: of(Arrays.asList("a", of(1, 2), 3L)) equals of(Arrays.asList("a", 1L, 2L, 3L)) and prints ('a',1,2,3). An empty list gives an empty tuple.

of(java.util.List) throws IllegalArgumentException when the list is null, when any element is null (e.g. Arrays.asList("a", null)), or when any element is not a String, Number or ComparableTuple (e.g. a list holding new Object()).

compareTo compares the tuples position by position up to the shorter length and returns the result of the first position that differs. Two strings compare with String.compareTo (case-sensitive), so the raw String.compareTo difference may be returned. Examples: of(1, 2) < of(1, 3); of("b", "a") > of("a", "z"); of("a", 5).compareTo(of("a", 5)) == 0.

At the same position a number is always smaller than a string, whatever their values: of(5).compareTo(of("a")) < 0, of(999).compareTo(of("0")) < 0 and of("0").compareTo(of(-5)) > 0. The result for such a mixed position is exactly -1 (number on this side) or 1 (string on this side).

When all shared positions are equal, the shorter tuple is smaller (-1) and the longer one larger (1); equal lengths give 0. So of("a") < of("a", "b") and NIL is smaller than every non-empty tuple, e.g. NIL.compareTo(of(0)) < 0.

Two numbers at the same position compare first by their long values (truncated toward zero) and, only when those are equal, by their double values; the result is -1, 0 or 1. Integer and floating numbers therefore compare by value: of(2L) equals of(2.0), of(2.5) > of(2L) and of(2.5) < of(3L); numbers of any Number class from the List factory compare the same way.

A NaN element has long value 0 and its double comparison is never equal, so comparing a NaN against any number whose long value is 0 (including another NaN, or 0, or 0.5) returns 1 from both sides (as the original does, this breaks the Comparable contract); of(Double.NaN) is not equal to another of(Double.NaN), though an instance equals itself. Against numbers with a non-zero long value NaN behaves like 0.

equals is true for the same instance, and otherwise only for another ComparableTuple whose compareTo result is 0; it is false for null and for objects of other classes. Thus of(2L).equals(of(2.0)) is true, and of("a", "b") equals of(new String[]{"a", "b"}).

hashCode starts at 0 and for each element in order multiplies the running value by 31 (int arithmetic, wrapping) and adds the element's hash: String.hashCode() for strings and Double.hashCode of the doubleValue() for numbers. Equal tuples such as of(2L) and of(2.0) therefore have equal hash codes, and NIL has hash code 0.

toString returns the elements in parentheses, separated by commas without spaces; strings are wrapped in single quotes without any escaping, numbers use their own toString. Examples: of("x", 7, "y") gives ('x',7,'y'); NIL gives (); of(1.5) gives (1.5); of(2.0) gives (2.0); of(Arrays.asList("a", of(1, 2), 3L)) gives ('a',1,2,3).

NIL is a shared tuple with no elements: it prints as (), has hash code 0, equals any other empty tuple (such as of(new String[0]) or of(Collections.emptyList())) and sorts before every non-empty tuple.

info(source, message) writes the text source + " " + message at INFO level to the wrapped org.slf4j.Logger, and warn(source, message) writes the same text at WARN; the three-argument forms pass the Throwable along with the text. The first message for a source key is always written. The logger's enabled levels are not consulted before throttling.

After a message for a source key is written, further messages for the same key arriving within the interval (elapsed System.nanoTime() difference less than or equal to the interval) are dropped and counted. info and warn share one throttle per key; different keys are independent. The default interval is 5 minutes; the two-argument constructor sets it in nanoseconds.

When a message for a key is written again after some were dropped, a summary line is written first: "<count> info log entries from <source> were not shown" at INFO if the first call ever made for that key was info, or "<count> warnings from <source> were not shown" at WARN if it was warn. The count is then reset to 0; no summary is written when nothing was dropped.

reset() forgets all source keys: the next message for any key is written at once and pending dropped counts are discarded without a summary line. setInterval(long) changes the suppression interval (nanoseconds, unvalidated) for all keys from the next message on.

new I18nText(key, args...) stores the key and a new array of the arguments in which null stays null, any java.lang.Number is kept as the same object and every other object is replaced by its toString() text (e.g. a StringBuilder "a" becomes the String "a"). Calling it with no arguments stores an empty array; passing a null varargs array throws NullPointerException. The no-argument constructor leaves both key and arguments null.

getI18nKey returns the key and getArguments returns the stored array itself (not a copy). setI18nKey replaces the key without checks, and setArguments stores the given array as is (no copying and no normalization; null allowed).

Two I18nText objects are equal when they have exactly the same runtime class, equal keys (null equals null) and argument arrays equal element by element (null array equal only to a null array). new I18nText("k", 1, "a") equals new I18nText("k", 1, "a") but not new I18nText("k", 1L, "a") (Integer 1 vs Long 1). Equal objects have equal hash codes (computed in the 17/37 style of Apache Commons Lang HashCodeBuilder).

toString returns the key alone when the arguments array is null or empty (null when the key is null); otherwise the key immediately followed by the arguments joined with commas, null arguments as empty text: key a.b with arguments x and 1 gives a.bx,1; key k with arguments null and x gives k,x.
I18nText binds to JSON with Jackson through the properties i18nKey and arguments: the main constructor is the Jackson creator for these two properties, and the getters expose them for serialization.

new IndexedForest(forest) wraps the forest without copying (a null forest throws NullPointerException). size() is the forest size, getForest() returns the same forest instance, depth(i) and row(i) return the forest's depth and row ID at position i (out-of-range positions fail like the forest's accessors). The forest must not change while the index is used.

subtreeEnd(i) returns the position just past the last descendant of row i, i.e. the first later position whose depth is not greater than row i's depth, or size() if none. For rows [1,2,3,4] with depths [0,1,1,0]: subtreeEnd(0)=3, subtreeEnd(1)=2, subtreeEnd(2)=3, subtreeEnd(3)=4. Any negative position returns size(); a position at or beyond size() throws an index exception.

parent(i) returns the position of row i's parent, or -1 if row i has depth 0 or i is negative. For depths [0,1,1,0]: parent(1)=0, parent(2)=0, parent(0)=-1, parent(3)=-1. For depths [0,1,2,1]: parent(2)=1 and parent(3)=0.

firstChild(i) returns i+1 when that row exists and is exactly one level deeper than row i, else -1; firstChild(-1) returns 0 for a non-empty forest and -1 for an empty one; other out-of-range positions give -1. nextSibling(i) returns subtreeEnd(i) when that position exists and has the same depth as row i, else -1 (also -1 for a negative position or one at or beyond size()). For depths [0,1,1,0]: firstChild(0)=1, firstChild(1)=-1, nextSibling(1)=2, nextSibling(2)=-1, nextSibling(0)=3, nextSibling(3)=-1.

children(i) returns a com.almworks.integers.IntIterator over the positions of row i's direct children in forest order (empty for a leaf or an out-of-range position other than -1); children(-1) and roots() iterate the positions of the top-level rows. childrenRows(i) returns the children's row IDs (not positions) as a new LongList, or LongList.EMPTY when there are none. rows(indices) lazily maps each position from the given IntIterator to its row ID.
root(i) returns the position of the top-level ancestor of row i (i itself when row i has depth 0); a negative i is returned unchanged. For depths [0,1,2,0,1]: root(2)=0, root(4)=3, root(3)=3.

IndexedRowTree.create(forest) returns a new tree holding the whole forest under its super-root (same order and nesting, so toForest() reproduces the rows and depths). getNodeWithRowId(id) returns the node for that row ID, the super-root for ID 0, and null for an ID not in the tree; hasRow(id) tells whether a node with that ID is in the tree and is false for 0.

Nodes added later through insertNode or appendForest become findable by row ID. remove(node) unregisters the node and all of its descendants: afterwards hasRow is false and getNodeWithRowId returns null for each of them. moveNode keeps the moved nodes registered.

Row IDs must be unique: creating a second node with an ID already in the tree raises AssertionError when Java assertions are enabled; without assertions the new node silently replaces the old one in the lookup.
new IndexedRowTree() and new IndexedRowTree(size) create empty trees (only the super-root); size is only a capacity hint, and a negative size throws IllegalArgumentException.

isMutuallyExclusive(LongList, LongList) is true when the lists share no value (order and duplicates do not matter) and true when either list is empty; e.g. [1,2] and [3,4] give true, [1,2] and [2,5] give false. The lists are not modified; null lists throw NullPointerException.
isMutuallyExclusive(LongSet, LongSet) is true when the two sets have no common value, including when either is empty, and false otherwise; null sets throw NullPointerException.

new ItemDisplayable(description, url) stores both values unchanged and without checks; getDescription() and getUrl() return them (url may be null). There are no setters and no custom equals, hashCode or toString (identity semantics).

new JavaListToLongListAdapter(list, f) is a read-only LongList view: size() is the source list's current size and get(i) applies f to the source element at i on every call (nothing cached), so later changes to the source list show through. An out-of-range index throws what the source list throws (typically IndexOutOfBoundsException). Other LongList operations (iteration, toNativeArray, equals) work through these two methods.

The static getters (getProjectManager, getIssueManager, getConstantsManager, getVersionManager, getOptionsManager, getUserManager, getGroupManager, getUserUtil, getPluginAccessor, getPermissionManager, getApplicationProperties, getAvatarManager, getComponentClassManager, getGlobalPermissionManager, getProjectComponentManager, getJiraAuthenticationContext) and getComponent/getComponentOfType return null when Jira cannot provide the service, otherwise a dynamic proxy implementing the requested interface that forwards to the service. The proxy is cached per interface class, shared by all these methods: later calls return the same proxy until the cache is cleared.

Each call on a returned proxy runs with the calling thread's context class loader set to the class loader of the real service object, restored afterwards even when the call fails; an exception thrown by the service is rethrown as is (not wrapped).

getOSGiComponentInstanceOfType(interface) looks up an OSGi service and returns it wrapped in the same kind of class-loader-switching proxy, or null if none; this result is not cached, every call creates a new proxy.
clearCaches(), afterPropertiesSet() and destroy() all empty the shared proxy cache, so the next lookups wrap freshly obtained services; clearUserCaches(user) does nothing.

withThreadContextClassLoaderOf(object, code) runs code.call() with the current thread's context class loader set to the loader of object (if object is a Class, that class's loader; otherwise the loader of its runtime class, null for bootstrap classes), returns its result, and always restores the previous context class loader, also when code throws; the exception propagates unchanged. A null object throws NullPointerException before the code runs.

Every JiraFunc property extractor (for example PROJECT_ID, PROJECT_KEY, ISSUE_ID, ISSUE_KEY, ISSUE_SUMMARY, ISSUECONSTANT_ID, PROJECTCONSTANT_NAME, USER_KEY, LABEL_LABEL, OPTION_ID, LINK_ID) returns null for a null argument and otherwise the corresponding getter value of the Jira object (which may itself be null). ISSUETYPE_SUBTASK is the exception: it returns Boolean.FALSE for null and otherwise whether the issue type is a sub-task type.

Some constants declare their result class so that La.array works: PROJECT_ID, PROJECT_KEY, PROJECT_DESCRIPTION, PRINCIPAL_NAME, GROUP_NAME, FIELD_NAME, ISSUECONSTANT_ID, ISSUECONSTANT_NAME, ISSUECONSTANT_NAME_LOCAL, VERSION_ACTIVE (Boolean), VERSION_SEQUENCE, VERSION_PROJECT, the PROJECTCONSTANT_* constants, ISSUE_PROJECTID, ISSUE_PRIORITYID, ISSUE_RESOLUTIONID, ISSUE_STATUSID, ISSUE_SUMMARY, ISSUE_DESCRIPTION, ISSUE_ENVIRONMENT, ISSUE_KEY, ISSUE_ORIGINAL_ESTIMATE, ISSUE_REMAINING_ESTIMATE, ISSUE_TIME_SPENT, ISSUE_TOTAL_TIME, ISSUE_VOTES, ISSUE_WATCHES, USERKEY_APPLICATIONUSER, the ISSUE_ASSIGNEE/REPORTER/CREATOR constants and their *ID forms, the four Timestamp constants, LABEL_LABEL, SECURITY_LEVEL_ID, SECURITY_LEVEL_NAME and OPTION_ID. Others, such as PROJECT_NAME, ISSUE_ID, ISSUE_WORK_RATIO and ISSUE_ISSUETYPEID, declare none, so La.array on them throws UnsupportedOperationException.
USER_NAME and APPLICATION_USER_NAME both map an ApplicationUser to its display name (not the login name); USER_KEY maps it to its user key.

VERSION_ACTIVE returns TRUE for a version that is not archived and FALSE for an archived one (null for null). NEGATED_ISSUECONSTANT_SEQUENCE returns the negated sequence of an issue constant, null if the constant or its sequence is null. ISSUETYPE_NAME and ISSUECONSTANT_NAME_LOCAL return the translated name, ISSUECONSTANT_NAME the raw name.

ISSUE_TOTAL_TIME returns the issue's time spent plus remaining estimate, a missing one counting as 0; it returns null when both are missing, when the sum is 0 or negative, or for a null issue (e.g. spent 3600 and no estimate gives 3600).
OPTION_NAME returns the option's value, or for an option with a parent option the parent's value, " - ", then the option's value (e.g. Europe - France); null for null.
GENERICVALUE_LONG_ID and GENERICVALUE_STRING_ID read the field id of a GenericValue as Long or String; null input or any exception during reading gives null.

KEY_PROJECT, ID_PROJECT, ID_ISSUETYPE, ID_STATUS, ID_PRIORITY, ID_RESOLUTION, ID_COMPONENT, ID_VERSION and ID_OPTION look the object up through the corresponding Jira manager (obtained via JiraComponents) on every call and return null for a null argument without querying; ID_COMPONENT also returns null when Jira reports the component as not found. USERKEY_APPLICATIONUSER resolves a key through JiraUsers.byKey.

ISSUE_ISSUETYPEID, ISSUE_PRIORITYID, ISSUE_RESOLUTIONID and ISSUE_STATUSID return the ID of the issue's type, priority, resolution or status (null if the issue or the constant is null). ISSUE_ASSIGNEE, ISSUE_REPORTER and ISSUE_CREATOR map an issue to the ApplicationUser of its assignee, reporter or creator key (null when the key is null).
VALID_ISSUE_KEY returns its argument unchanged when Jira's key syntax check accepts it as an issue key, otherwise null (null for null); it does not check that the issue exists.
CANONICAL_VERSION_NAME maps a Version to CoreIdentities.canonicalVersionName of its name; a null version gives null.

accessibleBy(user, permission) returns a predicate on Project that is FALSE for null and otherwise asks Jira's permission manager (fetched once at creation) on every call whether the user (null = anonymous) has the permission on the project; it declares Boolean as result class. If no permission manager is available it returns a constant-false function (AssertionError with assertions enabled). browseableBy(user) is accessibleBy with the browse-projects permission.

hasCustomField(field) returns a constant-false function for a null field. Otherwise it returns a predicate on Project that is FALSE for null, TRUE for every project when the field is configured for all projects, and else TRUE only for projects whose IDs were in the field's associated projects when hasCustomField was called (a snapshot).
byKey(null), from(null), getKeyFor((User) null), getKeyFor((ApplicationUser) null) and toDirectoryUser(null) all return null.

For non-null input, byKey, from and getKeyFor(User) return Jira's own user conversion result while the thread context class loader is temporarily set to the loader of Jira's user classes and restored afterwards (also on exceptions); getKeyFor(ApplicationUser) and toDirectoryUser call Jira's conversion directly without switching.

copyParameters(params, allowNull, makeImmutable, verify) with a null or empty map returns null if allowNull is true, otherwise an immutable empty map if makeImmutable is true, otherwise a new mutable empty map. A non-empty map gives the same result as mergeParameters(makeImmutable, verify, params).

mergeParameters(makeImmutable, verify, maps...) returns a new insertion-ordered map with the entries of all maps in argument order; a later map's value replaces an earlier one's for the same key while the key keeps its first position; null maps and a null varargs array are skipped. Values are deep-copied. With makeImmutable the result and all nested lists and maps are unmodifiable (UnsupportedOperationException on change); otherwise all are mutable.

With verify true, mergeParameters throws IllegalArgumentException with message "null key" for a null key, "non-string key: <key>" for a non-String key, and the checkValidParameter error for an invalid value.

copyParameter(value, makeImmutable) converts org.json JSONArray/JSONObject values to plain lists and maps, copies lists into new ArrayLists and maps into new insertion-ordered maps whose keys become String.valueOf(key), recursively; any other value (including null) is returned as the same object. With makeImmutable the new lists and maps are unmodifiable.

checkValidParameter accepts String, Integer, Long, Double and Boolean values and lists and String-keyed maps of such values (recursively, JSONArray/JSONObject converted first). It throws IllegalArgumentException with message "null value" for null, "invalid value type: <class name>" for other types (Float, Short, BigDecimal included), "invalid map: non-string key <key>" for a non-String key; nested errors are wrapped as "invalid list: invalid value at index <i>: <inner>" or "invalid map: invalid value for key <key>: <inner>" with the inner exception as cause. A cyclic or too deep structure gives message "stack overflow".

unwrapJsonCollection turns a JSONArray into a java.util.List and a JSONObject into a java.util.HashMap (recursively, JSON null becoming Java null) and returns any other value unchanged; a conversion failure becomes IllegalArgumentException with message starting "failed to convert json object: ". jsonToList and jsonToMap do the conversion directly and throw NullPointerException for null.
La implements java.util.function.Function and Predicate: apply(x) returns la(x) and test(x) returns accepts(x).

accepts(x) is true when la(x) is truthy: non-null and not equal to Boolean.FALSE, Integer 0 or Long 0. So results Double 0.0, Short 0, the empty string and TRUE are accepted; null, FALSE, 0 and 0L are rejected.
La.adapt(f) returns a La that calls the java.util.function.Function f; a null f throws NullPointerException.

La.constant(r) returns a function always returning r (null allowed). constant(Boolean.TRUE) returns the same shared instance as constantTrue() and constant(Boolean.FALSE) the same as constantFalse(); these return TRUE and FALSE for every argument.
La.isEqual(v) returns a predicate whose result is TRUE when v.equals(argument); for a null v it is TRUE only for null arguments.

La.inCollection(c) is TRUE when c.contains(argument), seeing later changes to c, and a constant-false function for null c. La.instanceOf(cls) is TRUE for non-null instances of cls, constant false for a null class. La.cast(cls) returns the argument when it is an instance of cls and null otherwise; for a null class it always returns null.

La.compose(g, f) returns x -> g.la(f.la(x)) (null intermediate results passed through) and throws NullPointerException if either is null; the result declares g's result class. h.apply(f) equals compose(h, f) and h.supply(g) equals compose(g, h).

La.self() is a shared identity function. La.notNull() is a shared predicate giving TRUE for non-null and FALSE for null arguments. La.stringValue() maps an object to its toString() and null to null, declaring String as result class. La.notNull(la, onNull) returns la's result or onNull when that is null, keeps la's result class, and throws NullPointerException for a null la.
La.fromMap(map, rClass) returns a function giving map.get(argument) (null when absent, live view of the map) with rClass as declared result class; a null map throws NullPointerException.

filter(Iterable) returns a new ArrayList of the elements, in order, that this function accepts (empty for null). filter(Iterator) returns a lazy filtering iterator (empty iterator for null). filterIterable(Iterable) returns a lazy Iterable that filters a fresh source iterator each time it is iterated (empty for null).

hashSet(c) and linkedHashSet(c) return a new HashSet/LinkedHashSet of this function's results for all elements, including null and falsy results, duplicates collapsed (LinkedHashSet in first-occurrence order); a null collection gives an empty set.

arrayList(Collection) and arrayList(Iterator) return a new mutable list of the results of all elements in order, falsy and null results included; null input gives a new empty list. arrayList(from, false) leaves out non-truthy results. arrayList(T...) maps the varargs the same way, but for a null or empty array it returns an immutable empty list.

iterator(Iterable) and iterable(Iterable) give lazy views of the results, computed on each next(); remove() is forwarded to the source iterator; a null source gives no elements. transform(Iterator) and transformIterable(Iterable) are lazy mapping views too, but a null source fails with NullPointerException when used.

La.longList(c, f) returns a new LongList of f's results that are non-null and strictly positive, in order (zero, negative and null results dropped), and LongList.EMPTY for a null or empty collection. La.intList does the same for Integer results, returning IntList.EMPTY for null or empty input.

addTo(from, to, acceptFalsy) adds the result for each element of a collection or iterator to `to` in order, skipping non-truthy results when acceptFalsy is false, and returns `to`; a null source adds nothing.

array(c) and array(c, acceptFalsy) return a new array whose component type is the function's declared result class, with the results in order; with acceptFalsy false, non-truthy results are dropped and the array is shortened. A null collection gives an empty array. If no result class was declared, UnsupportedOperationException is thrown (even for null input); if the collection yields more elements than its size() reported, IllegalStateException.

mapInto(c, map) puts result -> element for each element, mapInto(c, map, valueFn) puts result -> valueFn(element); elements whose key is null are skipped, later duplicates overwrite earlier ones, and the given map is returned. hashMap(c) / hashMap(c, valueFn) return a new HashMap and linkedHashMap(c, valueFn) a new LinkedHashMap built the same way; null collections give empty maps.

indexOf(list, sample) and lastIndexOf(list, sample) return the first/last position whose result equals sample (null matches null), or -1 if none or the list is null. find(c, sample) returns the first element whose result equals sample (null matches null), or null if none or the collection is null or empty.

any(iterable) is true when at least one element is accepted, stopping at the first one, and false for null or empty input. not() returns a predicate that is TRUE exactly when this function rejects the argument. and(second) returns a predicate that is TRUE when both accept, evaluating second only if this one accepts.
memoize() returns a non-thread-safe wrapper that calls the original once per distinct argument (by equals) and returns the stored result afterwards; null arguments and null results are cached too.

memoizeConcurrent() returns a thread-safe caching wrapper that calls the original at most once per argument in the absence of races; null arguments or null results throw NullPointerException (AssertionError when assertions are enabled). Null results are never cached.

comparator(cmp) returns a Comparator comparing two arguments by cmp applied to their results; a null cmp throws IllegalArgumentException with message "comparator is null". La.comparator(f) orders arguments by the natural order of f's results with null results first. La.LaComparator(function, comparator) throws IllegalArgumentException "function is null" or "comparator is null" for null arguments. La.ComparableComparator.compare returns 0 for two nulls, -1 if only the first is null, 1 if only the second is null, else b1.compareTo(b2).

liftToList() returns a function from an Iterable to the list of this function's results for its elements in order (all results kept): null maps to null, an empty iterable to an immutable empty list, otherwise a new mutable list.

image(c) returns a live read-only Collection view of this function's truthy results over c (non-truthy results skipped, duplicates kept); size() re-evaluates the function over the whole source each time; a null source gives an immutable empty list.

The La.FilterIterator returned by filter(Iterator) reads ahead: hasNext() advances the source until an accepted element is found and repeated hasNext() calls do not advance further; next() returns that element or throws NoSuchElementException when none is left; remove() always throws UnsupportedOperationException.

La.TransformIterator.hasNext() reports whether the source has more elements, next() returns the function's result for the next source element (possibly null), and remove() removes from the source iterator.
La2 implements java.util.function.BiFunction: apply(a, b) returns la(a, b). la(a1) returns a one-argument La that, given a2, returns la(a1, a2).
La2.sum adds two Integers with int arithmetic (overflow wraps, e.g. sum.la(2, 3) is 5); null arguments throw NullPointerException.
La2.uncurry(curried) returns a two-argument function computing curried.la(a1) and applying the result to a2; if curried.la(a1) is null, the result is null.

La2.const2(r).f() returns a two-argument function always returning r. La2.bind2(f).create() returns a two-argument function that ignores its first argument and returns f.la(second). The holder classes La2.Const and La2.Binder2 can also be created with their public constructors.
La3 is a La of its first argument: la(a1) (and therefore apply(a1)) returns a La2 that, given (a2, a3), returns la(a1, a2, a3).
La3.bind12(f).create() returns a three-argument function that returns f.la(a1, a2) and ignores the third argument; La3.Binder12 can also be built with its public constructor.

Limits holds int constants all equal to 190: MAX_MODULE_KEY_LENGTH, MAX_ITEM_STRING_ID_LENGTH, NODEID_MAX_LENGTH, MAX_SPEC_ID_LENGTH, MAX_NAME_LENGTH, MAX_USER_KEY_LENGTH and MAX_PATH_LENGTH. The class cannot be instantiated.

getMessageWithCauseChain(t) returns the toString() of t and of each cause in order, separated by "; ", e.g. "java.lang.IllegalStateException: x; java.io.IOException: y"; it returns the empty string for null.

warnExceptionIfDebug(log, message, t) logs at WARN: when DEBUG is enabled on log, message with t attached; otherwise, for non-null t, the text message + " " + the cause chain text without a stack trace; for null t just message.

A LongFilteringIterator yields, in order, only the values of the source LongIterator that pass the filter: with a java.util.function.LongPredicate those for which it returns true, with a La<Long, ?> those whose result is truthy. Filtering [1,2,3,4] with an is-even predicate yields 2, 4. The La constructor throws NullPointerException for a null filter.

split(iterator, filter) reads the whole source and returns a com.atlassian.jira.util.lang.Pair of two independent iterators over those values in order: first the accepted ones, second the rejected ones (e.g. [1,2,3,4] with is-even gives 2,4 and 1,3).

new LongListHashIndex(list) maps each value of the list to its position; indexOf(v) returns that position or -1 for a value not in the list, and size() is the number of distinct values. For a value occurring more than once the last occurrence's position is kept. Later changes to the list are not seen.
new LongListHashIndex(map) indexes an explicit value-to-position map, skipping entries with a null key, a null value or a negative value; indexOf returns the mapped position or -1.

new MapObject(JSONObject) wraps the given org.json object without copying (later changes show through); null is treated as an empty object. new MapObject(Map) builds a new JSONObject from the map. MapObject.from(obj) returns a MapObject for a JSONObject or a java.util.Map and null for anything else, including null. EMPTY is a shared instance with no keys.
isEmpty() is true when there are no keys; has(key) is true when the key is present; keys() iterates the current keys; get(key) returns the raw value or null when absent.

getObject(name) returns the value as a MapObject when it is a JSONObject or a java.util.Map, otherwise null (absent or other type). traverse(name) does the same but returns EMPTY instead of null, so chained lookups never fail.

getString(key) returns the value as text (a number 5 gives "5") or null when absent. getLong/getInt return the numeric value (numeric strings parsed) or 0 (or the given default) when absent or not convertible. getBoolean(key) is true for Boolean.TRUE or the string true in any case, otherwise false; getBoolean(key, default) returns the default when absent or not convertible. These follow org.json's lenient opt rules.

getLongList(key) and getIntList(key) return the numeric elements of the array under key in order (longValue()/intValue()), skipping non-numeric elements including numeric strings and nulls; a java.util.Collection value is treated like an array. A null key, an absent or non-array value or an empty array gives an immutable empty list.

getObjectList(key) returns the array elements that are JSON objects or maps, each as a MapObject; getRawObjectList(key) returns the raw elements skipping Java nulls; getStringList(key) returns elements as text; getList(key, extractor) applies the extractor to each index and keeps non-null results. transform(array, extractor) does the same for an array and returns an immutable empty list for a null or empty array. MAP_OBJECT_ARRAY_EXTRACTOR turns an element into a MapObject via from (null otherwise).

asImmutableMap() returns an unmodifiable map deep-converted from the JSON content (nested objects as maps, arrays as lists), built on the first call and cached; a top-level JSON null value makes it throw NullPointerException; JSON conversion errors become IllegalArgumentException starting "failed to convert json object:".

toString() returns the backing JSON object's compact JSON text. equals requires exactly the same class and backing JSON objects that are equal by JSONObject.equals; hashCode is the backing object's hashCode.

MapUtils.isSubMap(map, sub) is true when every entry of sub is present in map with an equal value (null values compared too); an empty sub is a sub-map of any map. E.g. {a=1,b=2} contains {a=1} but not {a=2} or {c=1}. Null arguments throw NullPointerException.

longOrZero(n) and doubleOrZero(n) return n's longValue()/doubleValue() or 0 for null. longOrNull(n) returns the same Long object if n is a Long, else a boxed longValue(), null for null; doubleOrNull likewise for Double. The (argument, function) forms apply the function first and return 0 (or null) without calling anything when the argument or the function is null.
nonNegativeLong and nonNegativeDouble return the value clamped to at least 0 (null counts as 0); nonNegativeDouble(NaN) stays NaN and -0.0 gives 0.0.

nonNegativeDoubleAddOrNull(a, b) is null if both are null, else the sum of the clamped values (null as 0). longAddOrNull(Number, Number) is null if both are null, the longValue of the non-null one if one is null, else the sum (wrapping, no clamping). longAddOrNull(long, Long) returns a when b is null, else a + b.
NumericFunctions.equals(a, b) is true when both are null, false when exactly one is, else a.equals(b), so Long 1 and Integer 1 are not equal.
Ref holds a value in the public field value: new Ref() holds null, new Ref(v) holds v, and the field can be read and assigned freely. toString() returns String.valueOf(value), i.e. "null" when empty.
A new RowTree contains only the super-root (row ID 0, flags 0, no children): toString() is the empty string and toForest() is an empty forest.

appendForest(forest) adds copies of all forest rows as new nodes with flags 0, the forest's top-level rows placed after the current last top-level node, keeping order and nesting. Appending a forest 1(2,3),4 to an empty tree gives toString() (1(2,3),4); appending forest 5 afterwards gives (1(2,3),4,5).

appendForest(forest, underNode, afterNode) places the forest's top-level rows as children of underNode right after afterNode, or before all existing children when afterNode is null. E.g. a tree (1(9)) with forest 2,3 appended under node 1 with afterNode null gives (1(2,3,9)).

The six-argument appendForest(forest, parentNode, afterNode, parentIndex, flags, rowFilter) copies the whole forest when parentIndex is negative, otherwise only the descendants of forest position parentIndex; copied top-level rows go under parentNode after afterNode (first if null), every new node gets flags, and a row rejected by a non-null rowFilter is skipped with its whole subtree. It returns the forest position just past the copied range (the forest size when copying everything).

insertNode(rowId, flags, parent, after) creates a leaf node and inserts it as a child of parent right after `after`, or as the first child when `after` is null, and returns it. moveNode(node, parent, after) detaches the node with its subtree and inserts it the same way, returning the node.
remove(node) detaches the node with its whole subtree from the tree; removing the super-root throws IllegalArgumentException with message "cannot remove super-root".
toForest() returns a new ArrayForest of all nodes except the super-root in depth-first pre-order, top-level nodes at depth 0, without flags; later tree changes do not affect it.

RowTree.Node.toString() returns the row ID when the node has no flags, else the row ID, # and the flags in decimal, e.g. 42 or 42#3. toFullString() (and append(StringBuilder)) gives the row ID (omitted for 0) followed, when there are children, by the children's full strings in parentheses separated by commas without spaces, e.g. 5(6,7(8)); flags are not shown.

RowTree.Node.hasFlags(mask) is true when all bits of mask are set (always true for 0); addFlags(mask) ORs the bits in. findFirstWithFlags(flags) returns this node or the first descendant in depth-first pre-order having those flags, or null.

RowTree.Node exposes getRowId, getParent (the super-root for top-level nodes), getFirstChild, getLastChild, getNextSibling and getPrevSibling (null when absent). getParent on the super-root or a detached node returns null, or raises AssertionError when assertions are enabled.

RowTree.Node.writeTo(rows, depths, depth) writes the subtree in pre-order: if depth >= 0 the node itself first with that depth, then each child with depth + 1; with -1 only descendants are written, children at depth 0. collectDirectChildren(collector) adds the row IDs of the direct children in order.

RunnableE.andThen(another) returns an action that runs this action and then another; if this action throws, another is not run and the exception propagates. A null another fails with NullPointerException only when the combined action runs, after this action has completed.
SpecParams.getObject(name) returns the nested value as a SpecParams when it is a JSON object or a java.util.Map, and null if it is absent or of another type.

getAttributeParameter(name, expectedFormat) reads an object under name with keys id, optional format and optional params and returns an AttributeSpec with that id, the params map (null if absent or not an object) and expectedFormat as format. It returns null when the object is missing, when both a stored format and expectedFormat exist and the stored one is neither expectedFormat's ID nor the ID of ValueFormat.ANY, or when the spec cannot be built (e.g. blank id or a colon in it). With a null expectedFormat the standard ValueFormat named by the stored format is used, and null is returned if there is none. getAttributeParameter(expectedFormat) uses the name attribute.

STRING_LONG parses a string as a decimal long after trimming whitespace (" 42 " gives 42) and returns null for null or unparsable text (decimals, out of range). INT_ITERATOR_TO_INT and LONG_ITERATOR_TO_LONG return the current value of an IntIterator/LongIterator without advancing it. MAX_PROPERTY_LENGTH is 250.

applyPermissions(rules, user, stack, resolver, pass) starts at pass and replaces the level by each rule's apply(user, level, stack, resolver) in order, returning the final level; a null rule list returns pass.

getSingleParameterLong(map, name) and getSingleLong(value) take the first element of a collection, Object[] or long[] (empty gives null); a Number gives its longValue(); a non-blank String is parsed as a long, falling back to double parsing truncated toward zero ("2.9" gives 2, "1e3" gives 1000); anything else, blank text or a missing key gives null; unparsable text logs a warning and gives null. A null map or name gives null.
getSingleParameterInteger reads like getSingleParameterLong but returns an Integer and gives null (with a warning) when the value is outside the int range.

getSingleParameterBoolean returns a Boolean value as is; otherwise it is true only when the single string value equals true ignoring case after trimming; missing values, a null map or a null name give false.

getSingleString(value) returns String.valueOf of the first element of a collection or String[] (null if empty), String.valueOf of any other non-null value (other arrays are not unwrapped), and null for null. getSingleParameter(map, name) is getSingleString of the map value, null for a null map or name.

getStringList(value) returns for a collection a new list of String.valueOf of its non-null elements; for a String[] a fixed-size list backed by the array (immutable empty if the array is empty); for null an immutable empty list; for anything else a one-element list of its text. getMultiParameter(map, name) applies it to the map value (empty list for null map or name). getMultiParameterLong parses each string with STRING_LONG into a new list, keeping null entries for unparsable strings.

getCommaSeparatedParameter(map, name, converter) splits the single string parameter at commas with String.split semantics (parts not trimmed, trailing empty parts dropped, e.g. a,,b, gives a, empty, b) and converts each part, returning a new list; a null or blank parameter gives an empty list.

setLongProperty(props, name, value) stores value (null as empty) in chunks of at most 250 chars under name, name.1, name.2, ... and then sets to null the following numbered entries while they hold non-empty values. getLongProperty(props, name) concatenates name, name.1, ... until the first missing or empty entry, returning an empty string if nothing is stored.
getBooleanSystemProperty(key, default) returns true only when the system property is set to true (any case), false for any other set value, and default when it is not set or the key is null or empty.
lastOrZero(list) returns the last element or 0 for null or empty. listsEqual(a, b) is true when both are null or empty, false when exactly one is, else element-wise equality.
copyPermissions(rules) returns a new list of clones of every rule in order (empty for null); copyPermissionsOrNull returns null for null and otherwise the same.

appendDebugIssueString(id, key, sb) appends (KEY ID), e.g. (ABC-1 10000), when the key is non-null and just the ID otherwise. getDebugIssueString(Issue) returns null text for null, else that label from the issue's key and ID. getDebugIssueString(Long) and appendDebugIssueString(Long, sb) give null text for null and otherwise look the key up via getDebugIssueKey, which returns null on any failure.
issueKeyOrId(issue, id) returns the issue's key when the issue is non-null, else "issue #<id>" when the ID is non-null, else "(no issue ID)".

appendDebugStructureString(id, manager, sb) appends the structure name in single quotes followed by " (#<id>)", e.g. 'Plan' (#12), reading the structure with security checks suspended; if loading throws StructureException it appends #<id>. getDebugStructureString returns the same text.

username(user) gives anonymous for null, the user's name, or user[name = null] if the name is null. debugConstant(c) and debugAction(a) give <null> for null and otherwise name(id), e.g. Bug(1). getDebugRowString(long) gives (row N); getDebugRowString(StructureRow) gives the row's toString() or the empty string for null.

getTextInCurrentUserLocale(key, params) returns JiraI18n.forCurrentUser().getText(key, params); the I18nText form uses its key and arguments (NullPointerException for null). getText(locale, user, key, params) uses JiraI18n.create(locale, user). getJiraDefaultLocale() returns Jira's default locale, or Locale.ROOT with a logged warning when it is not available.

getUserKey and getUserName return the user's key/login name or null for null; getGroupName returns the group name or null. getUserByKey resolves a key through JiraFunc.USERKEY_APPLICATIONUSER; getUserNameByKey returns that user's name or null; getApplicationUserByName asks Jira's user manager. migrateUserNameToUserKey lower-cases the name with Crowd's identifier rules (null gives null).
createRuntimeSignature() returns an int derived from the current time, the nanosecond timer and an identity hash code, varying between calls and JVM runs.

toJson(obj) serializes with a Jackson mapper omitting null properties and returns the empty string for null or on failure. fromJson(text, cls) and fromJson(text) return null for null or empty text and on parse failure (fromJson(text) also for non-object JSON). toMap(obj) converts a bean to a Map via Jackson (null properties omitted) and returns null on failure. toDebugJson(obj) returns the empty string for null, a String unchanged, otherwise JSON including null properties, or ?<error>? on failure.
onlyOneIsTrue(booleans...) is true exactly when one argument is true; false for none, for no arguments and for two or more.
swap(list, a, b) exchanges the elements at positions a and b in place; invalid positions throw IndexOutOfBoundsException.

getItemDisplayable(itemIds, service) loads the displayable text and URL attributes for all items in one request and returns a new map from each identity to an ItemDisplayable, using the identity's toString() when the text is missing or empty. The single-identity and StructureRow forms return the ItemDisplayable for that item (never null). getItemDescription(itemId) obtains the attribute service itself and returns the description, or null on any failure or when the service is unavailable.

StructureUtil's nn, nnv, lv, iv, lvn, ivn, nnl, nni, setType, mapType and listType behave exactly as the TypeUtils methods of the same names; isMutuallyExclusive as IntegersUtil's; isSubMap as MapUtils'; warnExceptionIfDebug and getMessageWithCauseChain as LoggingUtils'.
getBaseUrl() returns the base URL from the SAL application-properties service, the empty string if it reports null, and the empty string with a warning if the service is unavailable.

encodeURL encodes UTF-8 form-style (space as +, unreserved .-*_ kept, others %XX upper-case) and decodeURL decodes it; both return the empty string for null and decodeURL returns malformed input unchanged. encodeURIComponent writes spaces as %20 and leaves ! ' ( ) ~ unescaped, e.g. a b(c) gives a%20b(c).
isDevMode() is true when system property jira.dev.mode or atlassian.dev.mode equals exactly true (case-sensitive).
nonBlank(s) returns s trimmed; null, empty or whitespace-only input throws IllegalArgumentException with message "argument cannot be null or blank".

memoize(supplier) returns a non-thread-safe Supplier that calls the original only on the first get() and returns that same result (null included) afterwards; a supplier already returned by memoize is returned as is. If the first call throws, later calls return null without retrying (as the original does).

ToString.begin(name) returns a new StringBuilder with name followed by {; each append(sb, name, value) appends name=value, (for int, long, boolean and Object via String.valueOf) and returns the same builder; end(sb) removes one trailing comma (when the builder is longer than one char), appends } and returns the text. begin("Foo"), a=1, b=x, end gives Foo{a=1,b=x}; with no fields Foo{}. The String constants BEGIN, EQ, SEP and END hold the texts "{", "=", "," and "}".

TotalOrder.wrap turns Long, Integer, Short and Byte values into ComparableTuple.of(long) and Double and Float into ComparableTuple.of(double), so numbers of different classes compare numerically (compare(1, 1.0) == 0 and compare(2L, 1.5f) > 0); other non-string objects are kept as is; null stays null.

withStrictStringComparison compares strings with String.compareTo; withCaseInsensitiveStringComparison(locale) lower-cases strings with the locale (root for null or the no-arg form), so "ABC" and "abc" compare equal; withCollatorStringComparison(locale[, strength[, decomposition]]) and withCollator(collator) compare with a java.text.Collator (withCollator(null) behaves strictly).

COMPARATOR orders wrappers: null values last (two nulls equal); same runtime class by compareTo when Comparable, else by toString(); different classes put numbers (ComparableTuple) first, then String, then other classes by simple class name. So compare(5, "a") < 0, compare("a", null) < 0, and compare(Boolean.TRUE, new java.util.Date()) < 0 (Boolean before Date by name).

TotalOrder.ValueWrapper getValue returns the normalized value, getValueClass its class (null for null), isComparable whether it is Comparable, getOrder the producing order, toString String.valueOf of the value (e.g. (5) for 5). wrap(value, payload) returns a TotalOrder.PayloadWrapper whose getPayload is the payload and whose toString is the value text followed by the payload in parentheses, e.g. (5)(x).
setType(), mapType() and listType() return java.util.Set.class, java.util.Map.class and java.util.List.class.
nn(Long, long) and nn(Integer, int) return the value or the default for null; nnv(v, d) returns v or d for null; nn(String) returns "" for null; nnl and nni return 0 for null.
lv(s, d) and iv(s, d) parse a decimal long/int without trimming and return d for null or invalid text (" 5", "1.5", overflow); lvn and ivn return null instead.
fitsIntoInt(v) is true when v is within -2147483648..2147483647.
